subject: Mutual action plan & regional performance experiments — NovaPay evaluation and close timeline
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@novapay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan: regional perf evaluation & proposed close timeline

Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Per our conversation, I put together a concise Mutual Action Plan and evaluation outline so we can align on the tests NovaPay needs to validate production behavior and finalize procurement by the end of September. Attached: MAP_NovaPay_eval_plan.xlsx (single-sheet MAP) and test-script-samples.yaml (examples we will run).

High-level MAP milestones:
- Week 1 (Aug 24–28): test dev/staging runs — sanity checks and script tuning (Redwood runs).
- Week 2 (Aug 31–Sep 4): regional experiments (US, EU, APAC) with controlled traffic (Redwood + NovaPay).
- Week 3 (Sep 7–11): failover & multi-region routing stress (measure failover TTFT, route convergence, error modes).
- Week 4 (Sep 14–18): final perf sweep + signoff & procurement handoff; aim to close by Sep 30.

Evaluation plan (what we'll measure):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-region (token-level and request-level), end-to-end (edge->response).
- Throughput: sustained token/sec and requests/sec at target concurrency.
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): cold vs warm cache; cache warmup profiles.
- Concurrency: sustained concurrency levels and degradation curves.
- Failover: detection time, routing switchover, and tail latency impact on in-flight requests.
- Model variants: baseline (gpt-style base) and quantized variant for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Test constraints & success criteria we propose in the MAP:
- 99% of requests p95 < 400ms for US, p95 < 500ms for EU, p95 < 650ms for APAC during steady-state at target throughput.
- TTFT < 200ms warm cache; < 400ms cold.
- Failover detection & routing change < 5s; in-flight impact limited to increased TTFT not exceeding p95 SLO + 50%.

Logistics / asks for NovaPay:
- Please confirm the preferred test windows for each region and provide procurement contact for contract milestones.
- Share a short list of 5 representative prompt sets (we can redact PII) to use for quality parity checks.

If that plan looks good I can schedule dedicated test slots and loop in engineering to run an initial canary in EU first (per your note).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0172

Subject: NovaPay — EU canary results & cross-region summary (initial)

Ben / team —

Quick summary of the EU canary (Aug 31 09:00–12:00 CET) and the subsequent limited US/APAC sweeps we ran as part of the MAP runbook. Full CSV attached (novapay-summary-results.csv). This is an initial, non-finalized readout — we flagged a couple of items for follow-up below.

Key metrics (steady-state test traffic):
- EU (canary): p50 = 110ms, p95 = 380ms, p99 = 620ms; TTFT warm = 170ms, TTFT cold = 360ms. Sustained throughput: ~1,200 tokens/sec at concurrency target 40 (requests/sec 35).
- US: p50 = 95ms, p95 = 320ms, p99 = 510ms; TTFT warm = 150ms; sustained throughput: ~1,600 tokens/sec at concurrency 60.
- APAC: p50 = 170ms, p95 = 540ms, p99 = 880ms; TTFT warm = 210ms; sustained throughput: ~900 tokens/sec at concurrency 30.

Failover & routing observations (measured during simulated pod drain test):
- Detection + routing convergence: median 2.6s, 95th percentile 4.8s.
- In-flight requests: ~18% experienced increased TTFT; median increase +220ms, 95th +780ms.
- When a fallback model (quantized variant) was used to keep throughput, p95 latency increased by ~120–200ms but overall error rate remained <0.1%.

Action items we recommend:
1) Short-term: adopt a soft failover policy (route to quantized variant for up to 10s) to prevent request failures while limiting latency inflation.
2) Mid-term: tune per-region kernel selection (Karthik to lead) to lower APAC p95 by ~8–12%.
3) Procurement/sales: finalize reserved capacity numbers using the US sustained throughput profile as baseline with APAC as optional burst capacity.

Attachments: novapay-summary-results.csv (raw metrics), scheduled-run-notes.pdf (runbook notes). HubSpot link to the run record included in the MAP.

Next deliverable: detailed per-route dashboard and token-level breakdown by Sep 2 EOD. Let us know if you want a 30-min walkthrough this week; we can demo the cross-region traces and failover sequence.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
